audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items were 'Skill' and Level 6 was given to Sett — the exact inverse of the already-audited sett__warwick mirror on the one row that matters.
audit.why: Level 6 is Warwick's row: a 1.5s point-and-click suppression lands before Facebreaker or Haymaker can be cast. Every other stage is Sett's, because grit refills off the damage Warwick deals and his scaling beats Warwick's after items.
audit.corrected: Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Warwick, Sett, Sett — paired full/content rows with ratings 4/7/4/3 on the changed stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] claimed Warwick still out-duels Sett at first item, which contradicts both the new chart and the scaling story.
audit.why: Haymaker's shield scales with the grit Sett banks from Warwick's own sustained damage, so a longer fight after items feeds him rather than Warwick.
audit.corrected: First-item spike rewritten: his grit refills faster than you empty it; trade only inside the 18s after Haymaker is spent.
sources: Sett kit W text and cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker was written as a flat stun and Haymaker as a generic burst; no ability-level condition was given for either.
audit.why: Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — a solo laner standing on one side is slowed, not stunned. Haymaker's shield and true-damage core both come from banked grit, so the trade rule is about emptying the bar.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker's one-side-only-slows condition and 16s cooldown written into the cooldown list; the ult window keyed to an empty grit bar plus Facebreaker down.
sources: Sett kit E text and cd 16/14.5/13/11.5/10

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere (sequencingCues 0).
audit.why: Every trade rule said 'when it is down' without a number, so a player could not count.
audit.corrected: Haymaker 18s and Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 now appear in the cooldown block, the Do's and the spikes.

edits.after: Banked-grit Haymaker out-damages your burst trades through 4-5.

edits.before: Your Blood Hunt uptime and Q sustain still out-duel him at first item.
edits.after: His first-item Haymaker shield outlasts your Blood Hunt window.

edits.before: Infinite Duress locks him before he can land Facebreaker (E) grab or true-damage Haymaker; ult him when his W shield is empty and you win the all-in.
edits.after: Ult when his grit bar is empty and Facebreaker (E) is on its 16s cooldown — 1.5s of suppression is longer than he can survive with neither answer.

edits.before: Your Blood Hunt uptime and Q sustain still out-duel him after first items — just don't feed his W by trading into a full grit bar.
edits.after: After first items his grit bar refills faster than you can empty it — trade only in the 18s window after Haymaker (W) has been spent.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — His shield + true-damage burst. R after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker (18s at rank 1): matchup-defining — bait the shield, then commit inside that window. - Facebreaker (16s): alone on one side of him it only slows. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.after: His shield plus true damage — bait it, then engage in the 18s before it returns.

notes: Chart aligned to the already-audited sett__warwick mirror (Sett everywhere except Level 6). Note the tension for the user: Warwick still shows 52.67% over 860 games while the chart now gives Sett 6 of 7 stages — the mirror and the kit scaling both support Sett-by-stage, so the win rate is presumably coming from Warwick's global ult and jungle-adjacent play rather than the lane. Not asserted: whether Sett's own team can free a suppressed target, which the kits do not cover.
